newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: IMF hopes to solve Lithuania tariff dispute.
newsitem.headline: IMF hopes to solve Lithuania tariff dispute.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday that it was confident a solution would be found in its dispute with Lithuania over import tariffs.

Economy Minister Vincas Babilius said on Wednesday that Lithuania would refuse recommendations by the IMF that it further cuts its import tariffs as planned under agreements between the Fund and the Baltic state.
"We are talking and we are confident that we will find a solution," IMF resident representative in Lithuania, Domenico Fanizza, told Reuters.
Economy Minister Vincas Babilius on Wednesday said the main area of disagreement centred on tariffs on a group of agricultural products.
Lithuania has already cut these tariffs to 27.7 percent from 40 percent but the IMF wants a further reduction to 20 percent.
An IMF mission is in Lithuania to review how the Baltic state is performing under the terms of credits from the Fund.
Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius has said Lithuania cannot cut its import tariffs any more as domestic producers are already subject to too much competition.

The mission has also discussed Lithuania's plans to end its currency board system of keeping the litas pegged at four to one dollar although the central bank has said that the Fund has approved its plans to change monetary policy.
